I'm [music] Daniel Bley, foreign policy editor of LawFare with John Donnelly, author of Lifeline, the story of PEPAR, the greatest humanitarian initiative [music] of our time. So they went from clinic to clinic to clinic around a country setting up one or two rooms in that country that would they suddenly have an AIDS treatment program. They went and they had to purchase drugs. There was a race um among the embassies about putting in your drug orders fast because there wasn't enough supply to meet the demand, the new demand that this was creating. they would go and and start training laboratory technicians, doctors, nurses about setting how to treat AIDS patients all around these countries.
